title: 33.2 A 216-to-226GHz Watt-Level GaN Solid-State Power Amplifier with Multiband Large-Signal Impedance Correction and Circuit-Package Co-Design Technique
problem: 220GHz solid-state power amplifiers (SSPAs) are critical for future high-data-rate wireless, imaging, and radar; Si (CMOS/SiGe) and III-V (GaAs/InP) PAs suffer from low operating voltage (<2V single device), requiring low impedance at output (high current), limiting bandwidth and power density. GaN HEMTs offer higher voltage/current ratings but design is challenging at G-band.
motivation: 6G wireless, high-resolution imaging radar, and compact spectroscopy require compact, integrated 220GHz power sources with higher output power than current Si/III-V PAs. GaN's wide bandgap (higher voltage, higher current, higher frequency capability) enables new PA designs.
method: GaN HEMT-based 216–226GHz SSPA using: (1) multiband large-signal impedance correction to optimize output impedance across the G-band range despite device parasitics, (2) circuit-package co-design enabling efficient coupling from PA to antenna/load while managing thermal and parasitic effects.
key_novelty: GaN SSPA with multiband impedance correction and circuit-package co-design achieving watt-level output power at 220GHz.
contributions: GaN HEMT power amplifier operating across 216–226GHz (10GHz bandwidth, G-band)
Multiband large-signal impedance correction optimizing load-pull performance across frequency
Circuit-package co-design approach managing parasitic coupling and thermal distribution
Watt-level output power (specific power not provided in abstract)
Higher power density vs. Si/III-V approaches at same frequency
baselines: Si CMOS PAs (low voltage/power, moderate efficiency)
III-V GaAs/InP PAs (improved frequency but still voltage-limited)
limitations: Abstract does not specify output power in watts, power-added efficiency (PAE), gain, or noise figure. Bandwidth/efficiency tradeoffs not discussed.
